name: Tyrannosaurus Rex
facts: Had 60 teeth that were 8 inches long and the strongest bite of any land animal ever
Could grow up to 40 feet long and weigh over 15,000 pounds
The most complete T-Rex fossil 'Sue' has a skull that weighs 600 pounds alone

name: Triceratops
facts: Its name means 'three-horned face' with two giant brow horns and one on its nose
Grew nearly 30 feet long and weighed up to 5 tons
Could eat tough plants that other dinosaurs couldn't with its beak-like jaw and slicing teeth

name: Velociraptor
facts: Was actually the size of a turkey, not the giant monster from movies
Could run up to 24 miles per hour on its muscular legs
Had feathers covering its body like a deadly bird

name: Stegosaurus
facts: Had 17 kite-shaped plates along its back and dangerous spikes on its tail
Is the official state fossil of Colorado since 1982
Lived 155 million years ago and probably traveled in herds through wooded areas

name: Brachiosaurus
facts: Could reach vegetation 30 feet off the ground like a giant giraffe
Grew over 80 feet long and weighed more than 28 tons
Its front legs were longer than its back legs, making it stand tall and upright

name: Spinosaurus
facts: Was longer and heavier than T-Rex, possibly the largest carnivorous dinosaur ever
Had a giant sail on its back with spines the size of surfboards
Could swim and hunt fish like a crocodile with its long snout and straight teeth

name: Ankylosaurus
facts: Was covered head to tail in armor plates and had a massive bone club on its tail
Its name means 'fused lizard' because its skull bones were fused together like a helmet
Could swing its tail club hard enough to break the bones of attacking predators

name: Allosaurus
facts: Had 70 razor-sharp teeth and 8-inch-long claws for grabbing prey
Could run up to 21 miles per hour on two powerful legs
Was the most common large predator in its time, hunting stegosaurs and giant sauropods

name: Diplodocus
facts: Could grow up to 108 feet long - longer than 3 school buses
Its tail could crack like a whip at supersonic speed to scare off predators
Used its peg-like teeth pointing forward to strip leaves from plants like a living rake

name: Apatosaurus
facts: Laid eggs that were a whole foot long - bigger than a soccer ball
Had a brain the size of a baseball despite weighing 26 tons
Protected its babies from predators by hiding them in the center of the herd

name: Dilophosaurus
facts: Had two thin bony crests on its head that may have been used to attract mates
Could sprint at speeds up to 20 miles per hour chasing prey
Lived near rivers and streams in a wet, rainy environment 186 million years ago

name: Pachycephalosaurus
facts: Had a skull dome 10 inches thick - strong enough to headbutt rivals like a battering ram
Used its thick skull for head-butting contests, similar to bighorn sheep today
Lived in the last days of the dinosaurs and was one of the final species before the asteroid hit

name: Parasaurolophus
facts: Could produce loud, trumpet-like calls through its hollow 6-foot-long head crest
Grew over 30 feet long and weighed more than an elephant
Could walk on two legs or all fours and had a shovel-shaped beak for snipping tough plants

name: Carnotaurus
facts: The only meat-eating dinosaur with bull-like horns above its eyes for head-butting rivals
One of the fastest large predators ever, running up to 35 miles per hour
Had tiny arms even smaller than T-Rex, making it look like it had no arms at all

name: Giganotosaurus
facts: Bigger than T-Rex but had a brain the size of a banana!
Could run up to 31 mph despite being 43 feet long
Hunted giant titanosaurs - some of the biggest animals ever!

name: Therizinosaurus
facts: Had the longest claws of any animal ever - up to 3 feet long!
A vegetarian theropod - ate leaves instead of meat despite being related to T-Rex
Used its giant claws like hooks to pull tree branches closer to eat

name: Deinonychus
facts: The real-life 'Velociraptor' from Jurassic Park movies!
Had a huge sickle claw on each foot for slashing prey
Smart and fast - could run up to 25 mph and hunt in packs

name: Iguanodon
facts: Had a huge spike on each thumb - possibly for defense against predators
One of the first dinosaurs ever discovered back in 1822!
Scientists first thought its thumb spike was a horn on its nose!

name: Baryonyx
facts: Ate fish like a giant crocodile - fossils found with fish scales in its stomach!
Had a massive 12-inch claw on each hand for catching slippery fish
Also snacked on baby Iguanodons when it got the chance

name: Ceratosaurus
facts: Had a horn on its nose and two more above its eyes!
Had four fingers instead of three like most other theropods
The sprinter of the dinosaur world - could burst into high speed to catch prey

name: Albertosaurus
facts: Hunted in packs of 12 or more - teamwork made them super deadly!
T-Rex's smaller cousin from Canada
The most common big predator in Late Cretaceous Canada - the king of Alberta!
